open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-004 request decoding
open_points.text: “an import or request carrying its own status or project facts is refused at decoding” does not define which fields count as “project facts” beyond status.
open_points.question: Which request fields must decoding reject as client-supplied Registry context, and which ordinary project-related fields remain admissible?
options: Reject every Registry-derived field, including display name, address and customer reference.
Reject only lifecycle/validation fields such as status, exists and is_active.
Reject every field not explicitly declared by the request schema.
open_points.default_guess: Use closed request schemas and reject every undeclared field.

witness.initial: An active project exists and the caller otherwise passes authorization.
events: The caller submits a valid mutation request containing project_id and an extra display_name copied from Registry.
The decoder applies its interpretation of “project facts”.
outcomes: The request is refused before the Registry call because display_name is a client-supplied project fact.
The extra display_name is ignored or accepted because only lifecycle facts such as status are forbidden, and the mutation proceeds after live Registry validation.
witness.observer: The caller and the Registry gateway see whether the request is refused before a Registry call.

open_points.subject: INV-031 recognition decoding
open_points.text: “an unconfirmed, incomplete, unsupported-version or provider-carrying result is refused at decoding” and “no model or table carries a confidence, provider or raw field” do not define which input names or structures count as provider, confidence or raw fields.
open_points.question: What exact recognition input fields must be rejected as provider-specific, confidence or raw data, including unknown extensions?
options: Reject every undeclared recognition field.
Reject only a closed list of named provider, confidence and raw fields.
Permit and discard unknown fields unless they use specifically forbidden names.
open_points.default_guess: Reject every undeclared field at decoding.

witness.initial: A recognition publication is otherwise complete, confirmed and version 1.
events: An operator submits it with an additional provider_model field.
outcomes: The request is refused as provider-carrying and no table changes.
The unknown field is ignored because it is not one of the decoder's explicitly forbidden fields; the expense is created from the business fields.
witness.observer: The operator sees HTTP refusal versus successful expense creation.

open_points.subject: INV-027 budget derivation check
open_points.text: The added check says “no table has a derived-value column,” while State 1 requires persisted derived digests and hashes, including ApprovedEstimateSnapshot.content_fingerprint, Expense.intake_fingerprint and credential secret_hash fields.
open_points.question: Is the prohibition limited to editable or cached financial aggregates, or does it literally prohibit every derived value from persistence?
options: Only financial aggregates and budget-view values may not be stored.
No computed value of any kind may be stored, requiring removal of fingerprints and hashes.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the prohibition to financial aggregates and other read-view derivations.

witness.initial: No snapshot with the selected identity has yet been imported.
events: A producer publishes a valid snapshot.
The portal computes the content fingerprint required by M19 and A8.
outcomes: M19 and A8 require content_fingerprint to be stored so replay can be classified.
The literal new INV-027 check requires the table to have no derived-value column, so storing content_fingerprint fails the check.
witness.observer: The producer sees whether later identical publication is classified by the persisted fingerprint, and the verification check sees the schema difference.

open_points.subject: INV-028 activation refusal
open_points.text: “activating a budget version without an allocated section is refused” does not define “allocated section” and can mean either a version missing a section targeted by an allocation or a version having no section that currently receives an allocation.
open_points.question: Exactly which relationship between the candidate version's sections and existing allocations makes activation fail?
options: Refuse only when an existing allocation targets a PortalSection absent from the candidate version.
Refuse whenever the candidate version has no section currently targeted by an allocation.
Refuse whenever any candidate section has no allocation.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse only unresolved existing allocations whose target section is absent from the candidate version.

witness.initial: A project has an inactive budget version with one valid section, no expenses and therefore no allocations.
outcomes: Activation succeeds because there are no unresolved allocations, as State 1's activation rule says.
Activation is refused because the version is “without an allocated section” under the literal added check.
witness.observer: The staff caller sees activation success versus refusal.

open_points.subject: CLK-001 Required tests
open_points.text: CLK-001 includes equal operation timestamps, TTL-derived expiry, and preservation of source-supplied times, but its Required tests require only that multi-write operations have one equal instant, excluding audit occurred_at.
open_points.question: What Required tests demonstrate the TTL calculation and preservation/conversion of every source-supplied timestamp required by CLK-001?
options: Add checks for expiry = operation instant + TTL and for each source-supplied time retaining the same instant in offset-naive UTC.
Narrow CLK-001 to timestamp equality and state separate tested invariants for TTL and source-supplied times.
open_points.default_guess: Add focused checks for TTL derivation and source-supplied instant preservation.

open_points.subject: CLK-001 witness coverage
open_points.text: The Required tests demand “a test per multi-write operation (activation, revocation cascades, bootstrap),” but the only bound witnesses are service_identity_consumer_uow and staff_bootstrap; no witness is identified for budget activation or every revocation cascade.
open_points.question: Which existing witness check is bound to each activation and revocation-cascade test required by CLK-001?
options: Name a witness for budget activation and each cascade-owning operation.
State that the service-identity check covers a defined closed set of cascades and add the remaining witnesses.
Reduce the Required tests to the operations actually covered by the two named witnesses.
open_points.default_guess: Bind explicit witnesses for budget activation and every distinct cascade-owning operation.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 vulnerability authority
open_points.text: The rule uses “a public known-vulnerability database” and explicitly leaves “its tool, its database” to the deploy route, so whether a vulnerability is “known” depends on an undecided authority.
open_points.question: Which advisory source or deterministic combination of sources defines the closed vulnerability verdict for DEP-002?
options: One named public advisory database and snapshot format.
A defined union of named advisory sources.
Any deploy-route-selected public database.
open_points.default_guess: Use a defined union of named public advisory sources with a reproducible snapshot.

witness.initial: A built image contains a distribution version listed by public database A but absent from public database B.
events: The deploy gate scans the same image and version.
One implementation selects database A; another selects database B.
outcomes: The deploy is blocked because the version has a known vulnerability.
The deploy passes because the selected database has no advisory for that version.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees whether the same image is released.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 freshness limits
open_points.text: The test refers to “the deploy route's maximum snapshot age” and “its maximum environment age,” but neither value nor a rule deriving either value is decided here.
open_points.question: What exact max_snapshot_age and max_environment_age determine when otherwise valid vulnerability evidence becomes stale?
options: Fixed durations defined by the deployment policy.
Values supplied by deployment configuration with specified bounds.
No age-based reuse; obtain a fresh snapshot and verdict for every deploy.
open_points.default_guess: Define fixed deployment-policy durations and fail closed at the boundary.

witness.initial: The advisory snapshot and verdict for the exact image are 25 hours old and otherwise valid.
events: One deploy route uses a 24-hour maximum; another uses a 48-hour maximum.
outcomes: The deploy is refused as stale.
The same image starts because the evidence remains within the selected maximum age.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees refusal versus service start.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 Required test
open_points.text: DEP-002 says “no deploy ships an image” containing a listed vulnerable distribution, while its Required test only says the deploy step “starts the service only on a passing verdict.”
open_points.question: Must the gate prevent publishing or otherwise shipping the vulnerable image, or only prevent that image from starting as the service?
options: Prevent the image from being published or promoted as a deploy artifact.
Allow the image to be built and shipped to storage but prevent service start.
Define “ships” to mean starts the deployed service.
open_points.default_guess: Treat promotion to a deployable release as shipping and block it before publication or promotion.

witness.initial: A built image contains a distribution with a listed vulnerability.
events: The pipeline scans the image and receives a failing verdict.
The pipeline pushes the image to the deployment registry but does not start the service.
outcomes: The Required test passes because the vulnerable image never starts.
DEP-002 is violated because the deploy shipped the vulnerable image to the deployment registry.
witness.observer: The release operator and artifact-registry auditor see whether a vulnerable deploy artifact was shipped.
